_comment: Tier-2: exactly two ConstitutiveLawsApplication Python classes are absent from the string registry that Materials.json resolves against: SmallStrainKinematicPlasticityPlaneStrainVonMisesVonMises and FiniteStrainIsotropicPlasticityFactory. Pitfall (kratos.constitutive_laws #5). Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv). Both resolve as Python attributes while Kernel.HasConstitutiveLaw() is False for both — so the JSON route fails loudly while the Python-instance route reaches the solver. The isotropic sibling IS registered, which is what makes this a hole rather than a family-wide absence. The fixture imports KratosMultiphysics for real; with Kratos absent the import raises, the process exits non-zero and the runner records a failure, never a pass. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 INVERTS the expected outcome of all 5 probes -- it asserts the opposite of what this build actually does, while leaving each probe's callable untouched so every probe still really runs against Kratos. Every probe[...] line then disagrees with itself and probe_mismatches goes from 0 to 5. This proves the printed booleans come from actually calling into Kratos on this build, and that a wrong claim is caught, rather than the fixture echoing a hard-coded table. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS and these expect_in_output strings disappear: all 5 probe[<label>]=<ok>_expected=<must> lines, probe_mismatches=0. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/plasticity_two_registry_holes && /usr/bin/python3 source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 /usr/bin/python3 source.py (fails). Interpreter: KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 is REQUIRED on this host -- the repo venv Kratos wheel is built against GLIBC_2.32 and fails to load (ImportError on Kratos.cpython-312...so), while the system python3.8 carries Kratos 10.4 Release with CableNet, ConstitutiveLaws, StructuralMechanics and LinearSolvers.
